proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.8(i), first paragraph of the printed proof (pp. 44-45). No erratum.

Printed text: 'Observe first that if δ > 0 and if C₁, C₂, … are chosen with A ⊆ ∪_j C_j and diam C_j < δ for each j, then f(A) ⊆ ∪_j f(C_j) and diam(f(C_j)) ≤ (Lip f)δ < (1 + Lip f)δ. Hence H^m_{(1+Lip f)δ}(f(A)) ≤ Σ_j ω_m (diam f(C_j)/2)^m ≤ (Lip f)^m Σ_j ω_m (diam C_j/2)^m, and taking inf over all such collections {C_j} and then letting δ ↓ 0 we obtain H^m(f(A)) ≤ (Lip f)^m H^m(A). Notice this part of the argument is valid even if A is not H^m-measurable and did not depend on the σ-compactness of X.'

Conventions: the set is an arbitrary E ⊆ X; f : X → Y is only assumed K-Lipschitz on E; K plays the role of Lip f; and 𝓗^m := Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal m = c_m • μH[m] with c_m := realUnitBallVolume m / 2^m = ω_m/2^m ∈ [0,∞].

1. Covering argument for μH[m]. Let δ > 0 and let C₁, C₂, … be sets with E ⊆ ∪_j C_j and diam C_j < δ. Put C′_j := E ∩ C_j. Then f(E) = ∪_j f(C′_j). Since f is K-Lipschitz on E ⊇ C′_j, diam f(C′_j) ≤ K·diam C′_j ≤ K·diam C_j ≤ Kδ < (1+K)δ. Hence the size-(1+K)δ approximating sum of f(E) is at most Σ_j (diam f(C′_j))^m ≤ K^m·Σ_j (diam C_j)^m. Taking the infimum over all such covers and letting δ ↓ 0 gives μH[m](f(E)) ≤ K^m·μH[m](E). This is precisely Mathlib's LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le applied to h : LipschitzOnWith K f E and hd : 0 ≤ m, which yields μH[m] (f '' E) ≤ (K : ℝ≥0∞)^m * μH[m] E. It holds for every set E, every m ≥ 0 (including m = 0) and every K ≥ 0.
2. Normalization. By the definition of Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal, 𝓗^m = c_m • μH[m] as measures on X and on Y. So 𝓗^m(S) = c_m·μH[m](S) for every set S (Measure.smul_apply and smul_eq_mul in ℝ≥0∞).
3. Scaling. Multiplication by the fixed element c_m of [0,∞] is monotone, so step 1 gives 𝓗^m(f(E)) = c_m·μH[m](f(E)) ≤ c_m·(K^m·μH[m](E)).
4. Rearranging. Multiplication in [0,∞] is commutative and associative (mul_left_comm), so c_m·(K^m·μH[m](E)) = K^m·(c_m·μH[m](E)), which equals K^m·𝓗^m(E) by step 2.
5. Combining steps 3 and 4 gives 𝓗^m(f(E)) ≤ K^m·𝓗^m(E), which is the claim. No measurability of E and no σ-compactness was used.
key_steps: Covering argument: μH[m](f(E)) ≤ K^m·μH[m](E) for any E on which f is K-Lipschitz (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, needs 0 ≤ m).
Multiply by the constant ω_m/2^m and reassociate (mul_left_comm) to get 𝓗^m(f(E)) ≤ K^m·𝓗^m(E).
